texts.label: text
texts.orig: FGCN (Gao et al., 2022) constructs a heterogeneous food graph around users, recipes, and ingredients. It models ingredient-ingredient, ingredient-recipe, and recipe-user relations through multiple graph informationpropagation layers. Its experiments report improved food recommendation performance over the baselines considered in that paper and investigate data sparsity. FGCN is therefore a relevant baseline for food-entity representation learning, not a weak or obsolete model [9].

texts.label: text
texts.orig: GAME (He, Chow, and Zhang, 2020) learns graphical and attentive multi-view embeddings for occasional group recommendation. It aggregates information across group, user, and item views and uses neural collaborative filtering to model interactions. The paper reports improvements over its evaluated baselines, particularly for cold-start groups and items. CraveMap must therefore position its group mechanism as an extension toward operational dining constraints and persistent personal memory, not as the first solution to group cold start [2].

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The comparison is a capability and problem-scope comparison, not a claim that MTGCN is already more accurate. FGCN is specialised in high-order food-entity relations, while GAME is specialised in multi-view occasional-group recommendation. MTGCN proposes to combine and extend these ideas with multimodal evidence, dish-level taste attributes, dynamic context, persistent personal memory, and feedback. The expected advantage is broader functional coverage and better alignment with CraveMap's requirements. Whether this produces better ranking quality, group satisfaction, or long-tail discovery must be established experimentally.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: 7.5 Stage 5: MTGCN Representation Learning
texts.text: 7.5 Stage 5: MTGCN Representation Learning

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The proposed MTGCN processes the heterogeneous graph using relation-aware message passing and attention. Information is aggregated from connected neighbouring nodes. Relationship-specific transformations distinguish different types of connections, while attention weights determine the relative importance of neighbouring information. Contextual features are incorporated into the learned representations. The resulting user and dish embeddings are intended to capture food preferences at a more detailed level than cuisine labels or interaction frequency alone.
